analyzed_vuln.description: The root cause is missing validation of m_VersionOffset before using it as a pointer/length base. parseVersion() can set m_VersionOffset = -1 for malformed SIP request lines, but the constructor then does memchr(m_Data + m_VersionOffset, '\n', m_DataLen - (size_t)m_VersionOffset). Casting -1 to size_t underflows the length and creates an invalid pointer/huge read range, leading to wild read SEGV in memchr. Crash manifests in SipRequestFirstLine constructor, reached via SipRequestLayer creation.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: Fuzzer input is parsed as UDP payload on a SIP port in UdpLayer::parseNextLayer. If parseMethod() accepts the payload as a SIP request method but parseVersion() fails to find a valid version token (so m_VersionOffset becomes -1), constructor still executes the memchr search using that invalid offset. A malformed SIP first line in UDP payload is sufficient to trigger the crash when Packet parsing reaches SipRequestLayer.
